Undergraduate students who are accepted to participate as presenters in innovation-related competitions or industry showcases and/or tradeshows (henceforth: event) may apply for up to $1,000 in Innovation Travel Award funding.

Please read all rules, eligibility requirements, and application procedures below before applying. Note that the Innovation Travel Awards are not stipends or scholarships; students receive awarded funds after submitting reimbursement paperwork with supporting receipts.

Students are eligible for one Innovation Travel Award per academic year. At GT, an academic year is the combination of Summer, Fall, and Spring terms.

Students must book travel with Travel, Inc., GT’s contracted travel management company. This is an institutional requirement to comply with University System of Georgia business procedures. Click here for more information. Students: you must work with administrative personnel in your school or unit to book your air travel through Travel Inc. Travel Stipend Policy

To support participation in the CyAD Summit, June 23-25, 2026, a limited number of travel stipends are available to eligible attendees. The maximum stipend award is $1,500 and is intended to offset travel-related expenses. Stipends will be awarded based on estimated travel costs provided by the applicant and the availability of funds. Additional documentation may be requested prior to approval.

Applying for the stipend does not guarantee funding. Travel stipends will be awarded to approved registrants on a first-come, first-serve basis and may not last through the end of the registration period. If you are relying on the travel stipend to attend, then DO NOT incur any travel expenses before receiving approval. You will be notified via email if your request has been approved.

text:
Travel Grants Application | Academics | Utah Tech University

Utah Tech University

# Travel Grants Application

The Undergraduate Research Office (URO) Travel Grant Program provides funding opportunities to support travel expenses associated with student research, innovation, and creative activities. The goal of this program is to support student travel activities to present and collaborate on independent projects, or to access off-campus (non-local) sites to pursue their research and creative interests. Funding must be used to directly impact the proposed project, with the expectation that students will make significant progress on the project or engage in academic conferences in their related discipline. Awards are limited to $500 maximum for single applicant, or up to $1000 per project if 2 or more students are co-applying for this grant.

Rolling basis application until February 17, 2026. We aim to notify awardees a couple of weeks later.

Eligible expenses for projects include direct costs related to carrying out the proposed project such as attending academic conferences (including registration fees, travel, lodging, and associated per diem expenses) to present their work to a wider audience; to interact with collaborators on their research, innovative, or creative project; or to access off-site locations to collect data or other information from necessary sites. # The Office of Undergraduate Research and Major Awards

# Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship
The Office of Undergraduate Research and Major Awards offers the Undergraduate Research
Travel Fellowship to support undergraduate students from the University of Houston
in enhancing their academic development, disseminating their research results, and
increasing the visibility of the institution by supporting undergraduate student travel
at regional, national, and international conferences. The travel funding is intended
for undergraduates presenting the results of their research or creative activities
at meetings for a regional, national, or international audience within their academic
discipline.
**The Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship application is now closed for the 2024-2025
academic year. Please check back in August for the 2025-2026 URTF application.**
## Funding Offered
Students may apply for up to $500 to cover travel expenses associated with attending
and presenting their research or creative work at a conference.
The Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship may not cover all expected travel expenses.
Students are strongly encouraged to seek additional funding through research grants,
conference travel award programs, and awards offered by their department

## Community College Innovation Challenge (CCIC)Advancing Student Innovation & Impact

### Submissions Open: January 21, 2026Submission Deadline: April 3, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. PDT

### Check out a video on the CCIC here.

The Community College Innovation Challenge (CCIC) is led by the American Association of Community Colleges (AACC) in partnership with the National Science Foundation (NSF). It is a national competition where community college student teams, working with a faculty or administrator mentor, use science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) to innovate solutions to real-world problems; participate in an Innovation Boot Camp; and compete for cash awards.

AACC is pleased to announce that planning is underway to hold the Innovation Boot Camp in Washington, D.C. on June 8-11, 2026—and full travel support will be provided to the finalist teams to attend.

The Boot Camp provides professional development, mentoring, and coaching designed to build strategic communication and entrepreneurial skills to help students advance their innovations in both the private and public sectors. The event culminates in a poster session and engagement opportunity with STEM leaders and Congressional stakeholders, and a pitch presentation in front of a panel of industry and entrepreneurial professionals to determine the first, second, and third place winning teams.

# 2026 Global Student Conference Travel Grant

The Internal Audit Foundation is proud to offer the Global Student Conference Travel Grant to support students and educators from around the world in attending the 2026 Global Student Conference (GSC).

This opportunity provides financial assistance for flights, accommodations, conference registration fees, and/or visa support as needed, ensuring that participants can engage fully with their peers and industry leaders at this premier event.

This grant is designed to ensure global representation, with priority given to applicants demonstrating both geographic diversity and financial need.

## 2026 Global Student Conference will be held April 19-21, 2026 in Orlando, Florida

Applications for the 2026 conference have closed. 2027 GSC Travel Grant applications will open Q3 2026.

## Who can apply for the Global Student Conference Travel Grant

### Students

Preference will be given to:

- Students who hold a valid passport.
- Students in disciplines related to internal audit.

### Educators

Preference will be given to:

- Faculty who hold a valid passport
- Faculty interested in expanding internal audit education.
- Faculty who currently teach or research internal audit.

# AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars

The AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars Program empowers the next generation of innovators by providing resources, mentorship, and access to Grace Hopper Celebration.

2026 Applications coming soon!

## About the Kamala Scholars Program

The Kamala Scholars Program is a year-long opportunity made possible through the generosity of an anonymous donor, in honor of a family member, and is dedicated to opening doors and creating pathways for 3rd- and 4th-year undergraduate students pursuing technical computing fields. AnitaB.org offers many opportunities to elevate the full diaspora of our community. This particular scholarship is focused exclusively on Black and Latine students, in alignment with the donor’s wishes. Each year, we welcome 100 students into the program.

### Scholars receive:

1

### Travel, Lodging & Transportation

Fully funded travel, lodging, and transportation to attend Grace Hopper Celebration

2

### AnitaB.org Membership

One year of Premium AnitaB.org Membership

3

### Career Coaching Sessions

12 one-on-one career coaching sessions for professional growth

As part of their commitment, selected scholars are required to attend GHC 26 in Anaheim, October 27-30, 2026, participate fully in their coaching sessions, and complete required program surveys.
